item.title: Dispatched at -38°C: Surviving Sub-Zero Lock Freeze-Ups on Western Manitoba Farmlands
item.description: When the thermometer dips below -35°C on the open prairie between Brandon and the Saskatchewan border, physics changes the rules of locksmithing. Metal contracts. Moisture from a brief November thaw freezes into crystalline ice dams inside the pin chambers of mortise cylinders. And when a cattle rancher in Miniota or an ag equipment operator outside Virden needs entry to a heated workshop containing vital tractors, you don’t have the luxury of waiting for spring.

item.title: Anatomy of the Shear Line: Decoding Medeco Biaxial Cylinders & Angular Cuts
item.description:
When lock enthusiasts talk about “high-security” cylinders, the term is frequently tossed around as marketing jargon. But in the physical locksmithing realm, true high security (UL 437 rated) requires physical resistance against two distinct attack vectors: rotational shear line manipulation and sidebar deadlocking.

Among all classic pin-tumbler systems, the Medeco Biaxial remains one of the most elegant mechanical puzzles ever engineered. Today on Bench 01, we are breaking down a 6-pin Medeco Biaxial rim cylinder, exploring its chiral pin geometry, and demonstrating how rotational gating prevents traditional single-pin picking (SPP).

item.title: Manitoba Ag Days & Westman Maker Meetup: Modern Farm Security & GPS Anti-Theft Briefing
item.description:
Every year, thousands of agricultural producers, equipment engineers, and tradespeople converge on the Keystone Centre in Brandon, Manitoba for regional agricultural expos.

Earlier this month, our shop partnered with the local Westman Maker & Electronics Guild to deliver a live technical briefing on a rising threat across the prairie provinces: Targeted combine RTK GPS receiver theft and heavy machinery keyway vulnerabilities.

The Rising Threat: $15,000 Domes Stolen in 45 Seconds

Modern combines and high-clearance sprayers rely on precision GNSS/RTK receiver globes (StarFire, Trimble, Outback) mounted on the cab roof. A single receiver globe often costs between $8,000 and $18,000 CAD.

item.title: Prairie Telemetry: Deploying 915 MHz LoRaWAN Gate Sensors Across 4 Sections of Manitoba Ag Land
item.description:
One of the greatest security challenges for agricultural producers in Western Manitoba is distance. A modern multi-generation grain or cattle operation easily spans three to eight square miles (thousands of acres). Gateways, seed treatment sheds, and auxiliary chemical storage compounds are often miles away from the main homestead.

Cellular trail cameras frequently fail because rural cell towers don’t penetrate the deep Assiniboine River valleycoulees, and monthly multi-SIM data fees for 15 remote gates get exorbitant quickly.

item.title: Craft Log: Machining Custom 301 High-Yield Picks with Brass Ferrules & Manitoba Walnut
item.description:
In the trade, tools are an extension of your nervous system. When you are picking a serrated spool pin in a tight European keyway, your eyes can’t see the shear line; you are relying 100% on tactile friction and microscopic acoustic resonance transmitted up through the pick shank into your fingertips.

Most commercial mass-manufactured picks use cheap stamped steel with dipped rubber or plastic handles that dampen vibration. Over the past month in the wood and metal shop, I set out to produce a set of heirloom-grade tension tools and picks combining 301 High-Yield full-hard stainless steel, solid C360 free-machining brass bolsters, and salvaged Manitoba black walnut scales.

item.title: Bench Restoration: Resurrecting a 1912 Victor Safe 4-Wheel Pack from an Abandoned Prairie Credit Union
item.description:
In the early decades of the twentieth century, every booming railway town across Western Manitoba—from Souris to Minnedosa—had a solid brick bank or credit union anchored by a massive cast-iron safe. Built like battleships to withstand dynamite attacks from wandering train bandits, these safes housed mechanical combination locks that were marvels of Victorian hand-fitted precision.

Last month, during the demolition salvage of an old municipal hall north of Minnedosa, we were tasked with recovering and restoring an authentic 1912 Victor Safe & Lock Co. 4-Wheel Combination Lock.
